author: ansgar.eth
content: I have seen so many different proposals fly around for various acceleration variants (leanSPHINCS precompile, maybe ML-DSA precompile) and / or possibly some minimal block level aggregation variant.

author: ansgar.eth
content: or even whether we might expect wallets to opt out of mempool compatible frame txs if we don't have such a function, so they would have their own out-of-protocol aggregation layer, that would make their txs reliant on their own bundling / relaying

author: ivanlitteri
content:
One data point that may help frame this is that under 8141's current pricing, what a simple leanSPHINCS transaction pays is set almost entirely by the signature's bytes, not by how the signature is verified.

A leanSPHINCS signature is 7,740 bytes. 8141 prices those bytes at 16 gas per byte in the standard calculation, the usual price of a non-zero calldata byte, and at 64 gas per byte in the calldata floor (EIP-7976's values): ~124k and ~495k. A transaction pays the larger of the two, so a transfer ends up at ~0.5M gas whether the signature is verified natively (~13k of 515 Keccak permutations at KECCAK256's rate; this is a calculation, not a measurement, though) or in the EVM (~100-220k, measured in https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12644 for comparable hash-based verifiers, not leanSPHINCS itself). A leanSPHINCS precompile fixes node work and mempool eligibility (EVM verification doesn't fit `MAX_VERIFY_GAS`, 100k today), but not the price.

That leaves two real levers for "cheaper": price signature bytes differently from calldata, or remove them with aggregation. Both need the signature to be a separate object the protocol can bound, not bytes inside the transaction.

That is what the draft we propose in https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12672 does: the account declares the signature in a dependency frame (8288's interface), the signature travels beside the tx, and the block carries the list. Separate pricing becomes possible right away (not measured yet), and aggregation later only swaps the list for a proof, without changing accounts. It is also an in-protocol answer to the opt-out risk: wallets get a path whose cost drops later without moving to their own bundling layer

author: ivanlitteri
content: The cost is that it needs a transport (wrapper, a block field)

author: ivanlitteri
content: Which is not bad at all and is what we want in 8288 at the end of the day

author: ivanlitteri
content: The advantage of segregating the signatures from the tx is that if we do it now, then nothing has to change once we add aggregation
